questions.question: Village Q is to the North of village P. Village R is in the East of Village Q. Village S is to the West of village P. In which direction is village S with respect to village R?
questions.title: Directions — Village S relative to Village R
options: Both I and II follow (I as a valid…

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Place P at origin (0,0). Q is North of P → Q(0,1). R is East of Q → R(1,1). S is West of P → S(−1,0).
Direction of S from R: vector = S − R = (−2, −1) → negative x (West) and negative y (South).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: South-West.

questions.question: Statement: The number of fake currency notes circulating in the market has increased. Courses of Action: I. The police should form a special task force to track down the counterfeiters. II. Banks should be instructed to carefully verify all cash deposits.
questions.title: Courses of Action — fake currency notes increasing
options: Event A is the probable cause of Event B

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Both I and II follow** — forming a dedicated task force to catch counterfeiters (I) and instructing banks to verify deposits carefully (II) are both reasonable, practical responses to the stated problem.

questions.question: Statement: "Please do not use the lift in case of fire." Assumptions: I. While a fire breaks out, the lift is unsafe. II. The stairs are completely safe in case of fire.
questions.title: Assumptions — "Do not use the lift in case of fire"

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: An assumption is something implicitly taken for granted for the statement to make sense — check if the statement is meaningless without it.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Only Assumption I is implicit** ("the lift is unsafe during a fire" — this is exactly why the instruction exists). Assumption II ("stairs are completely safe") is too strong/unsupported a claim to be a necessary assumption.

questions.question: Statements: Some papers are files. All files are folders. No folder is a bag. Conclusions: I. No file is a bag. II. Some papers are folders.
questions.title: Syllogism — papers/files/folders/bag

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Some papers are files. All files are folders. No folder is a bag.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Since all files are folders, and no folder is a bag → no file can be a bag (Conclusion I: valid). Since some papers are files, and all files are folders → some papers are folders (Conclusion II: valid, via the chain).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Both I and II follow.

questions.question: A family consists of six members P, Q, R, X, Y, and Z. Q is the son of R but R is not the mother of Q. P and R are a married couple. Y is the brother of R. X is the daughter of P. Z is the brother of P. How many female members are there in the family?
questions.title: Family relations — counting female members

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Q is R's son, but R is NOT Q's mother → R is male (Q's father). P and R are married → P is female (R's wife). Y is R's brother → Y is male. X is P's daughter → X is female. Z is P's brother → Z is male. Q, being R's son, is male.
Females: **P and X** — Males: Q, R, Y, Z.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: 2 female members.

questions.question: Statements: Some lions are tigers. Some tigers are panthers. All panthers are cheetahs. Conclusions: I. Some cheetahs are lions. II. Some panthers are lions.
questions.title: Syllogism — lions/tigers/panthers/cheetahs
options: Neither I nor II follows definitively
questions.answer: Neither I nor II follows definitively

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Some lions are tigers. Some tigers are panthers. All panthers are cheetahs.

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Two consecutive "some" (particular) statements linked through a common middle term don't guarantee a valid conclusion, since the overlapping subsets referenced by each "some" statement may not actually intersect.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Neither I nor II follows definitively — the "some lions are tigers" subset and "some tigers are panthers" subset are not guaranteed to overlap.

questions.question: Statements: Some desks are caps. No cap is red. Conclusions: I. Some caps are desks. II. No desk is red.
questions.title: Syllogism — desks/caps/red

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Some desks are caps. No cap is red.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: "Some desks are caps" directly converts to "Some caps are desks" (valid conversion of a particular affirmative statement) → Conclusion I follows. Conclusion II ("No desk is red") is too broad — we only know about the desks that are also caps, not all desks.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion I follows.

questions.question: Statements: Only a few Managers are Leaders. All Leaders are Visionaries. No Visionary is a Follower. Conclusions: I. All Managers being Visionaries is a possibility. II. Some Managers are definitely not Followers.
questions.title: Syllogism — Managers/Leaders/Visionaries/Followers
options: Both I and II follow (I as a valid…
questions.answer: Both I and II follow (I as a valid…

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Only a few Managers are Leaders. All Leaders are Visionaries. No Visionary is a Follower.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Conclusion I ("All Managers being Visionaries is a possibility") — since it isn't contradicted by the given statements, it remains a valid *possibility* (not a certainty, but reasoning tests accept "possibility" conclusions when not ruled out). Conclusion II — since some Managers are Leaders, and all Leaders are Visionaries and no Visionary is a Follower, those Manager-Leaders are definitely not Followers.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Both I and II follow (I as a valid possibility, II as a certainty for at least some Managers).

questions.question: Statement: A severe cybersecurity breach has compromised the personal and financial data of millions of customers of a leading bank. Courses of Action: I. questions.title: Courses of Action — bank cybersecurity breach
options: Event A is the probable cause of Event B

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Only I follows** — freezing potentially affected accounts is a prudent, proportionate immediate response. Permanently shutting down the online portal and reverting to paper ledgers (II) is an extreme, impractical overreaction.

questions.question: Statements: All windows are doors. No door is a wall. Conclusions: I. Some windows are walls. II. No wall is a door.
questions.title: Syllogism — windows/doors/walls

sections.label: Given
sections.content: All windows are doors. No door is a wall.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Since windows ⊆ doors, and no door is a wall → no window is a wall, so Conclusion I ("Some windows are walls") is false, does not follow. Conclusion II ("No wall is a door") is the valid direct conversion of "No door is a wall" (E-type statements convert directly).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: In a certain coding language, the word 'MACHINE' is coded as 'LBBIHOD' by shifting letters alternately backward and forward by one step in the alphabet. Following the exact same alternating cipher pattern, how will the word 'NETWORK' be coded?
questions.title: Coded word — alternating cipher (backward/forward)

sections.label: Theory
sections.content:
From MACHINE → LBBIHOD, the shift pattern alternates: −1, +1, −1, +1, −1, +1, −1 (starting with backward on the first letter).
**Steps for NETWORK (N-E-T-W-O-R-K):**
- N(14) −1 → M(13)
- E(5) +1 → F(6)
- T(20) −1 → S(19)
- W(23) +1 → X(24)
- O(15) −1 → N(14)
- R(18) +1 → S(19)
- K(11) −1 → J(10)

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: MFSXNSJ

questions.question: A drone flies 15 km towards the North, then turns 135 degrees clockwise and flies 20 km. It then turns 90 degrees counter-clockwise and flies 10 km. In which general direction is the drone now pointing with respect to its original starting orientation?
questions.title: Drone direction after turns
options: Both I and II follow (I as a valid…

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Starts heading North (0°). Turns 135° clockwise → new heading = 0° + 135° = 135° (Southeast). Then turns 90° counter-clockwise → 135° − 90° = 45° (Northeast).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: North-East.

questions.question: Pointing to a lady, a girl said, "She is the daughter-in-law of the grandmother of my father's only son." How is the lady related to the girl?
questions.title: Relationship puzzle

sections.label: Given
sections.content: "She is the daughter-in-law of the grandmother of my father's only son."

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Since the speaker is a girl (female), "my father's only son" refers to her brother (not herself). The grandmother of her brother is the same as the girl's own (paternal) grandmother. The daughter-in-law of that grandmother is the wife of the grandmother's son — i.e., the wife of the girl's father.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The lady is the **girl's mother**.

questions.question: Syllogism: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are quadrilaterals. Conclusion: All squares are quadrilaterals. Does this follow?
questions.title: Syllogism: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are qu
options: Yes, it follows by chain (transitive) logic
Cannot be determined from the given data
questions.answer: Yes, it follows by chain (transitive) logic

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Two universal affirmative (All A are B, All B are C) statements chain transitively to give All A are C.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Yes, it follows** — since all squares are rectangles, and all rectangles are quadrilaterals, by transitivity all squares must be quadrilaterals.

questions.title: Directions: Rahul walks 10m North, then 10m East, then 10m S

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Track net displacement in each axis separately.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: North 10 then South 10 cancel out (net vertical = 0). Only the 10m East move remains.

sections.label: Answer
